newsitem.title: GERMANY: More hard times ahead for German retailers -- Ifo.
newsitem.headline: More hard times ahead for German retailers -- Ifo.

text.p: German retailers face little hope of crawling out of their most severe recession to date, said a top research institute, forecasting that sales would again fall this year.

The Munich-based Ifo economic research institute, saying Germany's fragile economic recovery continued to bypass the retail sector. It said retail sales would drop by a real one percent in 1997 after falling one percent last year and four percent in 1995.
"Germany has never seen such a long period of weakness in the retail sector," Ifo wrote in a report.
Fierce price competition would likely dent retailers turnover and raise the odds of more job cuts and insolvencies, Ifo said.
Investment is forecast to fall by about eight percent this year, Ifo said, adding, however, that livelier leasing activity might offset this drop.
As Germans prepare for summer sales beginning on Monday, retailers are keeping their fingers crossed that the traditionally frenzied two-week period will help the year's total turnover.

German law prohibits shopkeepers from reducing goods as they see fit and so department stores often slash prices by over 50 percent during the annual summer and winter sales as a last-ditch effort to move their wares.
But even considerable bargains have failed to shore up the retail industry in recent years as Germans have had less disposable income.
